headline: Head of National Conglomerate Steps Down After Realizing He Has Been Holding a Stapler in Meetings for Three Years
body:
The chairman of a major national conglomerate announced his surprise resignation today, citing a deep sense of personal embarrassment after discovering that the device he has been using to 'sign' official board documents for the last three years was, in fact, a standard office stapler.

'I kept wondering why my signature looked so metallic and jagged, but I assumed it was just a bold new font choice from the legal department,' the departing executive explained during a press conference held in the lobby of the corporate headquarters. 'It wasn’t until I tried to reload the ink cartridge and accidentally secured a merger agreement to my own left hand that I realized I might have been misusing the stationery.'

Junior analysts in the boardroom recalled several instances where the chairman would forcefully punch the stapler onto multi-million dollar contracts with a look of intense concentration. 'We all just thought he was really emphasizing his commitment to binding agreements,' said one management trainee who witnessed the signing of a major infrastructure project last November.

An interim board committee has been appointed to oversee the transition, with their first order of business being the collection of all office supplies within a five-meter radius of the executive suite. The outgoing chairman plans to spend his retirement attending a basic workshop on office equipment, with a specific focus on distinguishing pens from industrial fastening tools.
caption: A corporate exit takes a turn for the stationary after a three-year clerical misunderstanding. Who knew the difference between a pen and a stapler could shift the markets? #CorporateLife #OfficeHumor #Resignation (satire)
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a polished mahogany conference table featuring a pile of documents, a silver pen, and a stapler, with an empty leather office chair visible in the background.

sourceHeadline.title: N Chandrasekaran resigns as chairman of Tata Sons - Team-BHP

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Index 1 wins for the perfect balance of deadpan absurdity and relatable workplace tropes. The image of a high-level executive aggressively stapling contracts for three years is both highly specific and inherently affectionate in its depiction of corporate incompetence, avoiding cynicism while maintaining perfect AP-style structure.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a generic, fictional corporate executive to tell an absurd, harmless story. It does not name any real individuals, entities, or trending news events, and the image prompt is entirely generic.
